evals.prompt: I need meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B from HuggingFace for a local experiment. I already accepted the license on Hugging Face. Show me the exact startup command and curl request, and please call out any token requirement because I always get that wrong.
evals.expected_output: A gated HuggingFace download walkthrough that uses the current service startup flow, the correct API fields, and the correct port.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins huggingface.
Uses port 8200 for API calls.
Uses hub=huggingface and name=meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B in the request body.
Mentions HF_TOKEN or HUGGINGFACEHUB_API_TOKEN for gated access.
Shows how to capture or poll the returned job ID.

evals.prompt: I want sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 from HuggingFace and I want it pinned to the main revision so my CI job is reproducible. What request body should I use, and do I need a token for this one?
evals.expected_output: A public HuggingFace example that shows revision pinning and correctly explains that public models do not require a token.
expectations: Uses hub=huggingface and the exact model name.
Includes revision=main in the request body.
Explains that a token is optional for public models.
Uses the /api/v1/models/download endpoint on port 8200.
Avoids deprecated or made-up request fields.

evals.prompt: Download meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B and convert it into an OVMS-ready OpenVINO model for CPU with INT4 weights and a 4 GB KV cache. I need the exact request payload and the right plugins enabled.
evals.expected_output: A correct OpenVINO conversion workflow for an LLM, using the service's current plugin and config conventions.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins huggingface,openvino.
Uses hub=openvino, type=llm, and is_ovms=true in the request body.
Includes config.precision=int4, config.device=CPU, and config.cache_size=4.
Uses port 8200.
Explains where the converted OpenVINO artifacts will be written.

evals.prompt: Pull llama3.2:3b using the model-download service, not the raw ollama CLI. I always forget whether the tag belongs in name or revision, so please be explicit.
evals.expected_output: An Ollama walkthrough that uses the current API shape and clearly separates the base name from the tag.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins ollama.
Uses hub=ollama, name=llama3.2, and revision=3b.
Explicitly says not to send name=llama3.2:3b as a single field.
Uses port 8200.
Mentions that Ollama downloads are serialized.

evals.prompt: I need yolov8n with INT8 quantization for an edge demo. Give me the exact API payload and tell me what the quantize field is supposed to contain.
evals.expected_output: A supported Ultralytics request that uses a currently documented model name and explains how INT8 quantization is requested.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins ultralytics.
Uses hub=ultralytics with a supported model name such as yolov8n.
Includes config.quantize with a dataset value like coco128.
Uses port 8200.
Mentions that quantization is for a single model, not all or comma-separated names.

evals.prompt: I want the HLS 3D pose model for a healthcare analytics prototype. Show me the startup command, request body, and any model type field I need to set.
evals.expected_output: A focused HLS workflow that uses the correct plugin name, request shape, and supported healthcare model type.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins hls.
Uses hub=hls in the request body.
Identifies the type as 3d-pose.
Uses port 8200.
Mentions the other HLS model types rppg and ai-ecg.

evals.prompt: I have a trained model in Intel Geti and want to fetch it with this service. List the environment variables I need before startup and show me the request shape.
evals.expected_output: A Geti example that covers startup requirements, required environment variables, and the hub-specific request body.
expectations: Uses source scripts/run_service.sh up --plugins geti.
Lists GETI_HOST, GETI_TOKEN, and GETI_WORKSPACE_ID.
Uses hub=geti in the request body.
Uses port 8200.
Explains that the user still needs the relevant Geti identifiers such as model or project information.

evals.prompt: I’m brand new to this repo. How do I get the model-download service running locally, verify it is healthy, and know which plugin flag to use for HuggingFace versus Ollama versus OpenVINO?
evals.expected_output: A first-time setup walkthrough that matches the current startup script and gives practical plugin guidance.
expectations: Includes git clone and cd into microservices/model-download.
Uses source scripts/run_service.sh rather than raw docker compose as the primary path.
Shows curl http://localhost:8200/api/v1/health as the health check.
Explains at least huggingface, ollama, and openvino plugin choices.
Uses port 8200 consistently.
